title: School and university
summary: The school bell of the first of Mehr, uniforms and marks out of twenty, the dreaded konkur and student life at university – plus the words Iranians use when they talk about exams.

body.md: The Iranian school year begins on [[اول مهر|avval-e Mehr|the first of Mehr]], around 23 September, so in Iranian minds autumn and going back to school belong together. The first morning is a small festival: the youngest pupils, starting first grade, are welcomed with a [[جشن شکوفه‌ها|jashn-e shokufe-hā|'festival of blossoms']], school bells ring across the country, and the streets fill with children carrying a new [[کیف|kif|school bag]] and a pile of fresh [[دفتر|daftar|exercise book]]s. The year runs until early summer, when the exams of [[خرداد|Khordād|Khordad, May–June]] are followed by a long summer holiday.

Most schools are for girls or for boys only, and pupils wear a uniform: for girls a long smock, the [[روپوش|rupush|school smock]], with a headscarf, the [[مقنعه|maghna'e|school headscarf]]; for boys trousers and a shirt or jacket in the school's colours. Children spend six years at primary school, [[دبستان|dabestān|primary school]], and six at secondary school, [[دبیرستان|dabirestān|high school]], in two stages of three years. In many classrooms, when the [[معلم|mo'allem|teacher]] walks in, the class monitor, the [[مبصر|mobser|class monitor]], calls out [[برپا|barpā|stand up!]] and everyone rises.

Marks are given out of twenty. A [[نمره|nomre|mark]] of ten is a pass, and [[بیست|bist|twenty]] is perfect – so perfect that 'bist' also means 'excellent'.

At the end of school comes the [[کنکور|konkur|university entrance exam]], from French *concours*. A vast number of school-leavers sit it every year, and the [[رتبه|rotbe|rank]] they achieve decides which university and which subject they can enter; medicine and engineering at the top universities demand the very best ranks. For many families the final year is a marathon of private [[کلاس کنکور|kelās-e konkur|konkur prep class]]es and thick books of practice tests, and a student with a single-digit rank may be interviewed on the news. In recent years school grades have been given more weight in the result.

Iran's first modern college, the [[دارالفنون|Dār-ol-fonun|Dar ol-Fonun]], opened in Tehran in 1851, and the University of Tehran followed in 1934; its gate is one of the best-known images of the capital. Today almost every province has a public [[دانشگاه|dāneshgāh|university]], where the best-ranked students study free of charge, and the fee-paying [[دانشگاه آزاد|dāneshgāh-e āzād|Azad University]] has campuses all over the country. Students talk about their [[ترم|term|semester]], the number of [[واحد|vāhed|credit]]s they have taken, life in the [[خوابگاه|khābgāh|dormitory]] and, of course, their [[استاد|ostād|professor]]s.

Iranian schools are proud of their mathematicians, and Iranian teams do well at the International Mathematical Olympiad. The most famous of these students is [[مریم میرزاخانی|Maryam Mirzākhāni|Maryam Mirzakhani]] (1977–2017). As a schoolgirl in Tehran she won two Olympiad gold medals; after studying at Sharif University of Technology she went on to Harvard and Stanford, and in 2014 she became the first woman ever to win the Fields Medal, the highest honour in mathematics.

Exam talk has its own vocabulary. A student 'gives' an exam, [[امتحان دادن|emtehān dādan|to sit an exam]], and the teacher 'takes' it, [[امتحان گرفتن|emtehān gereftan|to set an exam]]. You hope to [[قبول شدن|ghabul shodan|pass]] and dread having to [[رد شدن|rad shodan|fail]] – or, as students say, to [[افتادن|oftādan|fall]] a course. The night before, [[شب امتحان|shab-e emtehān|exam eve]], is for cramming; the classmate who studies all the time is teased as a [[خرخون|khar-khun|swot]]; and everyone wants to know your [[معدل|mo'addel|grade average]].

sentences.fa: مدرسه‌ها در ایران از اول مهر باز می‌شوند.
sentences.r: madrese-hā dar Irān az avval-e Mehr bāz mi-shavand.
sentences.en: Schools in Iran open on the first of Mehr.
sentences.col: مدرسه‌ها تو ایران از اول مهر باز می‌شن.
sentences.colR: madrese-hā tu Irān az avval-e Mehr bāz mi-shan.

sentences.fa: برادر کوچکم امسال کلاس اول است.
sentences.r: barādar-e kuchak-am emsāl kelās-e avval ast.
sentences.en: My little brother is in first grade this year.

sentences.fa: فردا امتحان ریاضی داریم و من هنوز درس نخوانده‌ام.
sentences.r: fardā emtehān-e riyāzi dārim va man hanuz dars na-khānde-am.
sentences.en: We have a maths exam tomorrow and I still haven't studied.
sentences.col: فردا امتحان ریاضی داریم و من هنوز درس نخوندم.
sentences.colR: fardā emtehān-e riyāzi dārim o man hanuz dars na-khundam.

sentences.en: I got twenty out of twenty in the maths exam!

sentences.fa: او برای کنکور یک سال تمام درس خواند.
sentences.r: u barā-ye konkur yek sāl-e tamām dars khānd.
sentences.en: She studied for the konkur for a whole year.
sentences.col: اون واسه‌ی کنکور یه سال تموم درس خوند.
sentences.colR: un vāse-ye konkur ye sāl-e tamum dars khund.

sentences.en: What rank did you get in the konkur?

sentences.fa: خواهرم در دانشگاه تهران پزشکی می‌خواند.
sentences.r: khāhar-am dar dāneshgāh-e Tehrān pezeshki mi-khānad.
sentences.en: My sister studies medicine at the University of Tehran.
sentences.col: خواهرم تو دانشگاه تهران پزشکی می‌خونه.
sentences.colR: khāhar-am tu dāneshgāh-e Tehrān pezeshki mi-khune.

sentences.en: I've taken twenty credits this semester.

sentences.fa: شب امتحان تا صبح بیدار ماندم.
sentences.r: shab-e emtehān tā sobh bidār māndam.
sentences.en: The night before the exam I stayed up until morning.
sentences.col: شب امتحان تا صبح بیدار موندم.
sentences.colR: shab-e emtehān tā sobh bidār mundam.

sentences.fa: وقتی معلم وارد کلاس شد، همه بلند شدیم.
sentences.r: vaghti mo'allem vāred-e kelās shod, hame boland shodim.
sentences.en: When the teacher came into the classroom, we all stood up.
sentences.col: وقتی معلم اومد تو کلاس، همه پا شدیم.
sentences.colR: vaghti mo'allem umad tu kelās, hame pā shodim.

vocab.en: to pass (an exam); to be accepted
Mehr, the seventh month (late September to late October)

facts: The Iranian school year begins on 1 Mehr, around 23 September.
Iranian schools mark out of 20: 10 is the usual pass mark and 20 – bist – is a perfect score.
The word konkur comes from French concours, 'competition'.
The Dar ol-Fonun, Iran's first modern institution of higher learning, opened in Tehran in 1851; the University of Tehran was founded in 1934.
Maryam Mirzakhani, a graduate of Sharif University of Technology, became the first woman to win the Fields Medal, in 2014.
In Persian a student 'gives' an exam (emtehān dādan) and a teacher 'takes' one (emtehān gereftan).
Most Iranian schools are single-sex, for girls or for boys.
